title: Contract deviation scorecard and self-serve exception flow for MSA/DPA
creator: Rohan Patel
description:
Problem: Sales/CSMs and engineering customers repeatedly open tickets to request common deviations in our MSA/DPA (liability caps, indemnity language, data residency DPA clauses). Legal is a bottleneck and low-risk asks waste cycles. We need a defensible, auditable way to automatically approve low-risk deviations and route medium/high risk to the right reviewer.

Scope: Build a contract deviation scorecard (rule-based with ML augmentation later) that maps common redline requests and security questionnaire flags to a numeric risk score, surface a self-serve exception UI for account teams, and wire an approval routing flow (auto-approve, legal queue, CSM review, sales escalation). Add audit logging and dashboarding to measure approvals, time-to-approve, and revenue/velocity impact. Also map SIG/VSQ answers from customer security questionnaires to the same scorecard so security questionnaire work can auto-create or annotate contract exceptions.

Out of scope: Full ML model for clause classification (will be future work), changes to core MSA legal text without legal approval, DocuSign integration beyond metadata passthrough (phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard schema defined and stored in central config (JSON schema) and reviewed by Legal and Security
Mapping created for the top 25 most common redline requests and 10 security questionnaire flags to score components
Service endpoint returns a numeric risk score and suggested disposition (AUTO_APPROVE / LEGAL_REVIEW / CSM_REVIEW / SALES_ESCALATE) for a given request payload
Self-serve exception UI prototype in Console that allows Sales/CSM to submit a request with required metadata and shows suggested disposition
Legal queue shows recommended disposition, rationale, and provenance (questionaire answers, past exceptions) and can approve/override with a reason
Audit trail persisted (who requested, who approved, timestamp, decision, attached questionnaire or PR) and surfaced in per-account contract history
Metrics dashboard with conversion impact (avg time to close, % auto-approved, revenue impacted) available to product and legal
End-to-end happy path: low-risk deviation raised via UI -> auto-approve -> metadata recorded -> downstream Sign flow not blocked
decisions: Use a deterministic, rule-based scorecard initially (weights + flags) to ensure explainability to Legal and Sales
Score thresholds: 0-3 => AUTO_APPROVE; 4-7 => CSM_REVIEW/LEGAL_QUEUE (depending on clause type); 8+ => LEGAL_ESCALATE
Treat liability cap increases, third-party indemnity carveouts, and data export bans as high-risk automatically (base score +5)
Security questionnaire critical findings (encryption absent, no incident response) add +3 to overall score; low-risk findings add +1
Allow Legal to define an allowlist of customers (e.g., smaller customers or pilots) for broader auto-approve via configuration
Persist full justification with each decision, no silent auto-approves — system always records reason and actor
